questions.prompt: What is the main job of the large intestine?
options: Absorb water and salts from leftover food
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs water and salts from the leftover material and packs it into solid waste.
questions.misconception: Nutrient absorption happens in the small intestine - the large intestine's focus is water and waste.

questions.prompt: How does the large intestine compare in length with the small intestine?
options: It is exactly the same size
questions.explanation: The large intestine is only about 1.5 meters but much wider than the small intestine, which is why it is called 'large'.
questions.misconception: 'Large' means wide, not long - the small intestine is actually the longer tube.

questions.prompt: What do the friendly bacteria in the large intestine do?
options: Help process leftover material and make some vitamins
questions.explanation: Friendly bacteria in the colon process some leftover material and even make a few vitamins the body can use.
questions.misconception: These bacteria are helpers, not dangers - they are part of your healthy microbiome.

questions.prompt: Where is solid waste stored before it leaves the body?
questions.explanation: The rectum, the last part of the large intestine, stores the solid waste until it is released.
questions.misconception: Waste is not stored in the stomach or lungs - the rectum at the end of the large intestine holds it.

questions.prompt: What happens to most of the water that reaches the large intestine?
options: It is absorbed back into the body
It is always lost as waste
It stays in the colon forever
questions.explanation: The large intestine absorbs most of the water back into the blood, which is why the body does not lose huge amounts daily.
questions.misconception: The body is very efficient with water - nearly all of it is recycled here rather than wasted.
